editorial:
Imagine growing up with every toy and gadget you could ever want, but having parents who barely know your name. That is exactly the world you step into here. You follow a group of wealthy kids who seem to have it all on the outside, but inside, they are totally lost. It is a funny and sharp look at how money cannot fix a lonely heart. The vibe is a mix of high-society fancy and total teenage chaos, making you feel for these kids even when they are acting completely spoiled.

What really works are the performances because the actors make these bratty characters feel like real people. The pacing keeps you moving, and the jokes land well without feeling forced. If you like stories about rich people making bad choices, you will love this. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the kids finally stop pretending and confront their parents about their neglect. Instead of a huge fight, they find a way to bond over their shared sadness. The twist is that they realize their parents are just as trapped by their social status as the kids are. It wraps up with a hopeful note, showing that honesty is the only way they can actually start to heal their broken family ties.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories with a wealthy twist.
